title: AdapterManifest
description: Every adapter directory under adapters/<name>/ must contain a manifest.yaml validating against this schema, alongside its vector.toml (or equivalent collector config). The installer reads manifest.yaml to know how to wire the adapter into the ingestion pipeline without needing adapter-specific installer code — this is the mechanism that keeps adding a new data source a config change, not a product change.

adapter_name.description: Must match the directory name under adapters/. Used as the 'adapter' field stamped onto every canonical event this adapter produces.

vendor.description: Human-readable vendor/product name, e.g. 'CrowdStrike Falcon', 'Splunk Enterprise'.

protocol.description: How telemetry arrives at the collector. Determines which Vector/FluentBit source block the adapter's collector config uses.

port.description: Listening port, if input.protocol requires one (syslog, http_push).

auth.description: Authentication the collector must validate before accepting data from this source.

output_event_classes.description: Which canonical event classes (see schema/ocsf/) this adapter is capable of emitting. Used by the installer to sanity-check that ClickHouse tables/Qdrant collections needed by an enabled adapter actually exist before ingestion starts.

engine.description: Which log collector engine parses this source. Vector is the default; FluentBit is supported for sources where its plugin ecosystem is meaningfully better (Kubernetes-native sources, primarily).

config_path.description: Path, relative to the adapter directory, to the collector config file (e.g. 'vector.toml').

field_mapping_notes.description: Free-text documentation of any lossy or ambiguous field mappings from vendor-native format to canonical schema — e.g. how a 5-point vendor severity scale was collapsed onto the canonical 5-value enum, or which vendor fields have no canonical home and are preserved only in the raw blob. This is required in practice (even though not JSON-Schema-enforceable) because silent lossy mappings are exactly the kind of bug that surfaces mid-incident, not at adapter-authoring time.

maintainer.description: Who owns this adapter — 'airkit-core' for adapters shipped with the product, or a customer/team identifier for adapters authored locally.
